A line of characteristic impedance $Z_0$ with $v = c/√(ε_r)$ has phase constant $β = {2π}/λ$, with $λ = v/f$. If it ends in a load $Z_L$, part of the wave is reflected with the coefficient
La onda incidente y la reflejada forman: The incident and reflected waves form a standing wave: $|V|$ oscillates between $(1 + |Γ|)|V^+|$ and $(1 − |Γ|)|V^+|$, with a maximum every $λ/2$ and a minimum $λ/4$ later. The VSWR is the ratio between the two; it is 1 if the load is matched and grows without limit as it approaches a short circuit or an open circuit.
Z₀ sale de la geometría y del dieléctric: Z₀ comes from the geometry and the dielectric: coaxial $Z_0 = {η_0}/{2π √ε_r} ln(b/a)$ (≈ 60 ln(b/a)/√ε_r Ω); twin-wire $Z_0 = {η_0}/{π √ε_r} arccosh(D/2a)$; and in a microstrip $ε_{eff}$ lies between 1 and ε_r because part of the field travels through the air. Una línea de $λ/2$ repite la impedancia: A $λ/2$ line repeats the load impedance and a $λ/4$ one inverts it, $Z_"in" = Z_0^2/Z_L$. At a voltage maximum the impedance is real and equals $Z_0 "VSWR"$; at a minimum it equals $Z_0/"VSWR"$.
Es el plano del coeficiente de reflexión: It is the plane of the reflection coefficient $Γ$ (the inside of a circle of radius 1) with the normalized impedances $z = Z/Z_0 = r + j x$ drawn on top: the circles of constant $r$ and the arcs of constant $x$. The centre is $z = 1$ (matching), the edge is purely reactive loads, the point on the left is the short circuit and the one on the right the open circuit.
Desplazarse hacia el generador una dista: Moving toward the generator a distance $d$ is turning clockwise on the constant-VSWR circle (radius $|Γ|$) through an angle $4π d/λ$: a full turn every $λ/2$. Going from impedance to admittance is turning half a turn, $y = 1/z$.
<b>Stub en paralelo.</b> Se conecta en p: Shunt stub. A piece of short-circuited or open line is connected in parallel, at a distance $d$ from the load. $d$ is chosen so that there the normalized conductance is 1, $y = 1 + j b$ (the circle $r = 1$ of the chart read as admittances, that is, turned half a turn), and the stub length $l_s$ so that its susceptance is $−b$. There are two solutions. A short-circuited stub has $y_s = −j cot(β l_s)$ and an open one $y_s = j tan(β l_s)$.
<b>Transformador λ/4.</b> Donde la imped: λ/4 transformer. Where the impedance is real (a voltage maximum or minimum) a piece of line of length $λ/4$ and $Z_T = √(Z_0 Z_"real")$ is inserted, which takes it to $Z_0$.
